chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My grandfather narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Suleiman, that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
As for Al-Hasan, I have granted him grandeur and patience, and as for Al-Hussein, I have granted him benevolence and compassion.
ai.seo_question: What specific virtues did the Prophet grant to Imam Al-Hasan and Imam Al-Hussein?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the distinct spiritual and moral legacies of the two Imams, framing their virtues as divine endowments that define their respective roles in Shia theology. While Al-Hasan is associated with dignified patience (*haybah* and *hilm*), essential for political stability and quietude, Al-Hussein is linked to active generosity and mercy (*jud* and *rahmah*), reflecting his sacrificial stand at Karbala. This distinction underscores the complementary nature of their imamate, balancing serene authority with compassionate activism.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-124 Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Alavi - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his grandfather quoted Muhammad ibn Ja’far, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Safvan ibn Suleiman that the Prophet (MGB) said, “
RegardingAl-Hassan, I have granted him my grandeur and patience, and regarding Al-Hussein, I have granted him my benevolence and compassionateness.”
